review.summary: Follow-up review of the supplied changes only: the no-run orphan branch, the registration overlap classifier, the playback expectation change and the new tests. All four MINOR fixes and the NIT fix are in place and I found no BLOCKER or MAJOR issues. (1) With no run, every frame-bound page counts as an orphan and sets hasGap. (2) The overlap check (admittedAt < endAt AND settledAt??clockAt >= startAt) correctly catches registration requests admitted before the window that can still lose an in-window source, and correctly excludes requests that ended before the window, which the new tests cover. (3) Viewer/playback pending, failed, interrupted or missing frames still increment the counters but no longer set the registration visit gap, and the open-run unknown_history test can tell the two outcomes apart. (4) The wrong-kind check stays a global structural check outside the classifier. I accept the countermax rebuttal: values over 10k break the existing migration129 CHECK, so rejecting them is correct. One MINOR remains: the wrong-kind test doesn't show that wrong-kind alone causes evidence_gap. Caveats: tsc has not been rerun yet, the fixture fix for the real DB check is described but its code isn't shown, the mapping from status 'available' to sourceIngress.state 'no_run' isn't shown, and full five-metric readiness stays NOT_READY. An empty or minor-only findings list doesn't certify tests or release.

findings.file: reconcileMetricVisitSources test file (existing test file in the supplied scope; name not provided)
findings.area: New test 'reports wrong-kind bindings as structural contradictions outside the report window'
findings.issue: This test asserts evidence_gap and wrongKindSources:1, but unlike the isolated orphan test it doesn't assert that the other gap causes are absent (sealCountMismatch:false, orphanSources:0, missingSources:0). It uses the base sealed `run` fixture as-is, so the frame/page/playback seal counts may not match this one-frame, one-viewer-page dataset. If they don't, evidence_gap could come from a seal-count mismatch instead of the global wrong-kind check.
findings.evidence: database([wrong],[],[],context,[run],[outside]) with an unmodified `run` (counts not set for this dataset). The expectation lists only coverage.reason and wrongKindSources. In contrast, the orphan test sets pageCount:0 and checks missingSources:0 and sealCountMismatch:false.
findings.impact: The test may pass even if the wrong-kind check were removed from the global gap calculation, so the NIT/MINOR fix 'wrong kind remains global structural check' isn't proven in isolation.
findings.recommended_fix: Set the run seal counts explicitly to match the fixture (for example frameCount:1, pageCount:1, playbackCount:0, sealedAt >= 3600). Then add sealCountMismatch:false, orphanSources:0 and missingSources:0 to the toMatchObject expectation.
findings.required_test: Rerun the wrong-kind test with the explicit isolation assertions. Optionally, temporarily disable the wrong-kind contribution to hasGap and confirm the test then fails.
